children: AMMAN — The Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO) has conducted training workshops in Tafileh and Maan on the safe and sustainable use of treated wastewater in agriculture.

The workshops brought together farmers, civil society representatives and officials from relevant national and local institutions under the Building Resilience to Cope with Climate Change in Jordan through Improving Water Use Efficiency in the Agriculture Sector (BRCCJ) project.

The sessions focused on using treated wastewater for agricultural irrigation, including suitable crops, irrigation practices, water quality requirements, and relevant legal and regulatory provisions, according to an FAO statement.

Participants also discussed social and cultural considerations related to the use of treated wastewater and the role of civil society organisations in raising awareness about its safe and responsible use.

FAO Policy and Education Specialist Samia Akroush provided an overview of the BRCCJ project, its objectives and components, and efforts to improve water-use efficiency, promote climate-smart agricultural practices and strengthen the capacity of local communities and civil society organisations.
The workshops included field visits to wastewater treatment plants in Tafileh and Ma’an, where participants were briefed on treatment processes and plant operations.

They also received information on water-quality testing procedures and standards, treated-water storage and distribution systems, safety requirements, and the costs and fees associated with using treated wastewater.
The activities included a visit to a farm benefiting from treated wastewater, where participants observed the use of treated water to irrigate olive trees through a drip irrigation system.

The training involved 50 farmers and civil society representatives, four representatives from the Ministries of Agriculture, Water and Irrigation, and Environment, and four wastewater treatment plant staff members.

The BRCCJ project seeks to improve water-use efficiency in agriculture and strengthen communities’ capacity to adapt to water scarcity and climate change through knowledge exchange and practical training.

Funded by the Green Climate Fund and implemented by FAO in partnership with the Ministries of Water and Irrigation, Agriculture and Environment and the UN Development Programme (UNDP), the project is being implemented in Madaba, Karak, Tafileh and Maan within the Dead Sea Basin.
The project is aligned with the Economic Modernisation Vision and focuses on areas particularly vulnerable to climate change and water scarcity.

title: ZAWYA: Jordan: FAO holds workshops on treated wastewater use in agriculture
